draft.method: The route table and OpenAPI come from the draft application assembled in a throwaway environment with local placeholder settings (`contracts/tools/generate_draft_baseline.py`). Consumers were found by reading each client's source.

endpoints.auth_details: Bearer token in the `Authorization` header, or (browsers) in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` as `whisperer-bearer, <token>`. Query-string tokens are NOT accepted. No token, invalid token, or slot refusal -> `ws.close(code=1008)` BEFORE accept. Under uvicorn a pre-accept close is turned into an HTTP 403 Forbidden handshake response, so clients never see close code 1008 for auth failures. An exception inside _resolve_user (DB down, JWT_SECRET unset -> RuntimeError, signed JWT without `sub` -> KeyError) is not caught and becomes HTTP 500 from uvicorn. No error frame is sent.
endpoints.handshake: 1) Edge: nginx `location ^~ /v1/ws/` proxies to the `ws` process role (fallback `api`), proxy_read/send_timeout 3600s, retries the handshake on another upstream on HTTP 503 (drain). 2) DrainMiddleware (pure ASGI): if the drain marker file exists, the handshake is refused with HTTP 503 `draining` (websocket.http.response extension) or, without the extension, a pre-accept close 1013 (-> HTTP 403). 3) Handler: extract token (Authorization, else subprotocol); resolve user; on failure close 1008 pre-accept (HTTP 403). 4) Acquire WS slot (per-user Redis pool + per-worker counter); on refusal close 1008 pre-accept (HTTP 403). 5) `accept(subprotocol='whisperer-bearer' | None)`. 6) Server immediately sends `ready` {user_id, timestamp} unprompted. 7) Client normally sends `hello` (Swift/C# clients send `{"type":"hello"}` only); server answers with a second `ready`, then (if the transcription role resolves) `transcription.mode`. 8) Client sends `session.start` {session_id} to bind a meeting; server answers `session.ack` and, if a roll was found, `transcript.restore`. 9) Steady state: binary audio frames + `audio.commit`/`ask`/`ask.transcript`/`vision`/`answer.stop`/`ping`; the server streams `transcript*`, `answer.*`, `error`, `pong`. Text frames are handled inline in arrival order except `ask`, `ask.transcript`, `vision`, which run as background tasks (AnswerGate, max 2 concurrent per socket, oldest is cancelled with finish_reason `superseded`).
endpoints.protocol_version: There is NO protocol version field, negotiation or capability exchange. `hello` carries only optional `language` and `session_id`; unknown fields are ignored. Compatibility is achieved by additive evolution: new binary codes 2/3 were added beside 0/1, the server decides the audio mode and announces it with `transcription.mode` (clients that ignore it keep sending WAV chunks, which always work), new server frames (`transcript.restore`, `transcription.error`, `answer.suppressed`, `answer.stopped`) are designed to be ignored by older clients (shipped clients drop unknown types), optional `id` on answer frames, optional `trigger` on ask frames. `hello` may be sent any number of times and is not required (the first `ready` is sent without it). Evolution rule implied by the code: never rename existing types/codes/fields; only add.
endpoints.resume: No sequence-based replay. Each socket has fresh in-memory state (seq counter restarts at 1, answer ids restart at `a1`, history, restraint, quota cache). Reconnect resume is meeting-scoped: after reconnect the client re-sends `session.start` (or `hello` with `session_id`); the server re-binds the meeting after an ownership check and, only on `session.start`, restores the conversation roll from the Redis mirror `realtime roll` (TTL 30 min, max 20 000 utterances, appended per final utterance) or, if empty and the meeting is not ephemeral, from transcript_segments (max 2 000 rows). Restored utterances are treated as already answered and sent once as `transcript.restore` (after `session.ack`, trimmed from the head to ~512 KiB with `truncated:true`). Restore does nothing if the socket's roll is non-empty. `hello` with session_id binds but does NOT restore. Idempotency: `answer.stop` is idempotent (unknown/finished id -> count 0); `session.start` repeated is safe; ask/vision frames have no idempotency key (a resent ask produces a new answer). `transcript.seq` is per-socket, monotonic in audio arrival order with gaps allowed (empty/failed chunks), not a resume cursor. `session.end` drops the Redis mirror and triggers meeting post-processing. In-flight answers and transcriptions are cancelled when the socket closes (no terminal frame is sent then).

close_codes.when: No/invalid token. Sent as websocket.close BEFORE accept, which uvicorn converts to HTTP 403 at the handshake; the client never sees 1008.
Per-user slot pool full (ws_max_conn_per_user=8, shared with other non-translate WS channels) or per-worker cap (ws_max_conn_global=500). Pre-accept -> HTTP 403.

No client text/binary frame received for WS_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S=600 s (protocol-level ping/pong does not count). Preceded by an `error` frame with code `idle_timeout`. This is a real post-accept close frame.
Drain refusal when the server lacks the websocket.http.response extension; pre-accept so it surfaces as HTTP 403.

Handler returns after an unhandled exception in the receive loop (an `error` frame `internal` is attempted first, then the handler returns without ws.close; uvicorn's sansio impl closes TCP without a close frame). Version-dependent: the legacy websockets impl would send 1000 instead. Same path is hit by: a text frame that is valid JSON but not an object (e.g. `[]`, `1`, `null`) or whose `type` is unhashable (AttributeError/TypeError — NOT bad_json), and any exception raised by an inline handler (e.g. DB failure during hello/session.start ownership check, Redis/DB failure in session.end). Also any network drop.
Server shutdown (SIGTERM) while the socket is open: uvicorn sends close 1012. The app sends NO `server.shutdown` frame.

close_codes.when: Client did not answer a protocol-level ping within ws_ping_timeout (uvicorn default 20 s; not overridden in Dockerfile/compose).

Process is draining before shutdown; new handshakes only. nginx retries another upstream (proxy_next_upstream http_503).

frames.description: Optional greeting; can be sent any number of times. Sets the recognition language and optionally binds a meeting (ownership-checked, no roll restore). Server replies `ready` and then (best effort) `transcription.mode`. If session_id is not owned -> `error` forbidden (then still `ready`). Shipped clients send only {"type":"hello"}. Every hello re-sets language (absent -> auto). A meeting bound via hello does not load the meeting title (used in prompts) — only session.start does.

fields.name: language
fields.description: Speech recognition language. Trimmed, lower-cased; empty or "auto" (or non-string) means auto-detect per utterance (default). Stored for the socket; not the UI language.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description: UUID of an existing meeting owned by the user. Invalid/absent -> ignored. Not owned -> error `forbidden`. Binding here does not restore the roll.

frames.description: Application-level keepalive; resets the 600 s idle timer like any frame. Server replies `pong`.

Bind (or unbind) the active meeting: transcript segments, AI executions and the Redis roll mirror are attached to it. Ownership checked (IDOR). Owned/absent -> `session.ack`, then `transcript.restore` if a roll was restored. Not owned -> socket is UNBOUND (session cleared) and `error` forbidden is sent, no ack. Also used after every reconnect.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description: Meeting UUID. Absent/null/empty/unparseable -> explicit unbind (ack with session_id null).

frames.description: Meeting finished: if a meeting is bound, enqueue live-meeting understanding (notes/decisions) and delete the Redis roll mirror, then unbind. No reply frame.

Stream mode only: the client detected end of phrase for a speaker. The buffered PCM for that speaker is committed to the streaming ASR session in a background task (counts against the 3 in-flight transcription limit; silently dropped when saturated). Produces `transcript.partial`* then `transcript` (or nothing if empty, or `transcription.error`). seq is assigned at commit time. A commit dropped by the gate is not lost audio: the buffered PCM rolls into the next commit for that speaker. ASR/role failures surface as `transcription.error`, not `error`.

fields.name: speaker
fields.description: "me" (default when absent/empty); any other value is treated as "them".

frames.description: Typed or client-supplied question (chat, recap "what did I miss", system design). Runs in background. Context = whole meeting roll; does not move the answered/new-speech boundary. Flow: empty -> `error` empty_question (once) or `answer.suppressed` reason empty; unsafe -> `error` unsafe_request; known-exhausted quota -> `error` minutes_exhausted (once); rate cap -> `error` rate_limited; else `answer.start` -> `answer.delta`* [`answer.continue`] -> exactly one terminal `answer.done` or `error` (with id). NOTE: minutes_exhausted is told once per socket; every later ask/vision while exhausted gets NO frame at all (no answer.start, no terminal). An auto-triggered ask first passes the interjection gate (may yield `answer.suppressed`).

fields.name: question
fields.description: Question text; absent -> "" (then rejected as empty). Truncated to 128 000 chars.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: ""/absent = live answer (role `responses`, or `coding` if the question looks like code), "chat" (neutral assistant), "recap" (summariser), "system_design" (role system_design + Mermaid diagram contract). Unknown values behave like "".

fields.name: use_kb
fields.description: Truthy -> prefetch Knowledge Base (RAG) context. Default false.

fields.name: trigger
fields.description: "auto" (case-insensitive) marks an automatic suggestion: the server interjection gate may answer with `answer.suppressed` instead. Absent = manual request (never suppressed). Not sent by shipped clients.

frames.description: Answer the speech heard since the previous suggestion ("Ask" button / auto-answer). Question = new speech since the last boundary (rendered with timestamps); context = roll before it; the boundary then advances. Same reply sequence as `ask`.

fields.name: trigger
fields.description: "auto" -> subject to the interjection gate (may yield `answer.suppressed`).

frames.description: Screenshot(s) -> AI answer, background task. The only type allowed above 512 KiB (up to 12 MiB). Flow: known-exhausted quota -> `error` minutes_exhausted; unsafe prompt -> `error` unsafe_request; rate cap -> `error` rate_limited; else `answer.start` then deltas (reasoning always "" on the native-vision route) and one terminal frame; bad/no images -> terminal `error` bad_image; vision role unresolvable -> `vision_unavailable`; model without vision and no describer -> `vision_describer`.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: Question about the screenshot(s); falsy -> server default question (VISION_DEFAULT_QUESTION).

fields.name: images
fields.description: Array of base64 strings (raw or `data:<mime>;base64,` URL; the prefix is stripped). Non-string/empty items ignored. Preferred over image_base64 when it is a list. Max 6, each <= 8 MiB, PNG/JPEG/GIF/WEBP.

fields.name: image_base64
fields.description: Legacy single image, used only when `images` is not a list.

frames.description: Cancel generation. Handled inline (not queued behind answers). Idempotent. Server replies `answer.stopped`; each actually-stopped answer also emits `answer.done` with finish_reason "cancelled".

fields.name: id
fields.description: Answer id (e.g. "a3") to stop; absent/empty/non-string -> stop ALL live answers of this socket.

frames.binary_format: u8 speaker (0 me, 1 them) + RIFF WAV, PCM16LE mono 16 kHz
frames.description: Finished phrase as WAV (chunk mode; the only mode older clients know). Layout: byte[0] = speaker code: 0x00 = me (microphone), 0x01 = them (system audio). bytes[1..] = a complete RIFF/WAVE file, PCM16 little-endian; clients send 16 kHz mono (server reads rate/channels from the fmt chunk, accepts 8-48 kHz, 1-2 channels; falls back to 16 kHz mono for duration if the header is unparseable). Typical chunk ~0.8 s / tens of KB. Frames > 2 MiB are silently dropped; frames beyond 3 in-flight transcriptions are silently dropped. seq is assigned on acceptance in arrival order. Produces `transcript` (non-empty text only); ASR provider failure -> `transcription.error` (once per failure series); transcription role not configured -> `error` transcription_unavailable on EVERY chunk; quota exhausted -> `error` minutes_exhausted once per socket, then chunks are dropped silently; too fast -> dropped, one `transcription.error` audio_rate_exceeded per socket.

frames.binary_format: u8 speaker (2 me, 3 them) + raw PCM16LE mono at transcription.mode sample_rate (24 kHz), 200 ms frames
frames.description: Continuous-stream piece (only after the server announced `transcription.mode` mode="stream"). Layout: byte[0] = 0x02 = me, 0x03 = them; bytes[1..] = raw headerless PCM16 little-endian mono at the announced sample_rate (24 000 Hz), nominally frame_ms=200 ms (9 600 bytes). Appended inline (in order, not under the transcription gate) to the per-speaker streaming ASR session; nothing is returned until `audio.commit`. Frames > 2 MiB dropped. Unknown first byte (>=4) or empty frame: silently dropped. Quota/pace rules as for chunks; role or provider failures -> `transcription.error`.
Sent immediately after accept (unprompted) and again in reply to every `hello`.

How the client should send audio, decided by the server from the user's transcription model. Sent after the `ready` that answers `hello`, only when it differs from the mode already announced on this socket; silently skipped if the role cannot be resolved (client stays in chunk mode). Never sent on the initial unprompted `ready`.
Reply to `ping`.
Reply to a successful `session.start` (bind or unbind). Shape is frozen (restore data deliberately goes in a separate frame).

fields.name: session_id
fields.description: Bound meeting UUID, or null when unbound.

frames.description: Conversation roll that survived a disconnect, sent right after `session.ack` only when something was restored (never empty).

fields.name: truncated
fields.description: True when oldest lines were dropped to fit ~512 KiB.

fields.name: lines
fields.description: Utterances in chronological order (oldest kept lines first).

fields.name: lines.speaker
fields.description: "me" or "them" (DB fallback maps unknown labels, including the owner's display name, to "them").

fields.name: lines.at
fields.description: Wall-clock epoch seconds, rounded to 3 decimals.

frames.description: Final recognized utterance (chunk mode: per WAV chunk; stream mode: per audio.commit). Never sent for empty text. Delivery order can differ from seq order in chunk mode (up to 3 parallel recognitions); clients order by seq.

fields.name: speaker
fields.description: "me" or "them" (stable id, not the display label).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: Per-socket utterance number starting at 1, assigned at audio acceptance (chunk) or commit (stream); gaps allowed.

frames.description: Stream mode only: growing partial text of the phrase being committed (cumulative, not a delta). Never stored; followed by `transcript` with the same seq.

Speech recognition failure, deliberately NOT an `error` frame (clients would put `error` into the answer page). Provider failures are reported once per failure series (flag reset by the next successful chunk/commit); `audio_rate_exceeded` once per connection.

fields.name: code
fields.description: "audio_rate_exceeded", or str(LLMProviderError) from the ASR provider — an open set (e.g. "model_unavailable", "insufficient_balance").

frames.description: An answer to ask/ask.transcript/vision has started (sent before model resolution/prompt assembly). After it, exactly one terminal frame for this id follows (`answer.done` or `error` with id) unless the socket closes; exception: when the answer role cannot be resolved the `error` responses_unavailable is sent WITHOUT id and no answer.done follows.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Per-socket answer id "a1", "a2", … (unique within the connection only).

frames.description: Streamed answer text, coalesced (first delta immediately, then every 25 ms / 512 chars). After a content-filter hit, the buffered text is discarded and a delta carrying the localized refusal is sent followed by answer.done content_filter; because the provider stream is drained for usage, every remaining provider chunk re-sends the same refusal delta (quirk).

fields.name: content
fields.description: Answer text increment (may be "" when only reasoning arrived).

fields.name: reasoning
fields.description: Model reasoning increment ("" if none; always "" on the native vision route).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Answer id. Always present on this endpoint (the helper omits it only when no terminal/id exists, which this endpoint never does).

frames.description: The model hit max_tokens (finish_reason=length) and the server is auto-requesting a continuation (or a rescue pass if nothing was produced); further deltas of the same answer follow. Max 3 per answer.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Answer id (always present on this endpoint).

frames.description: Terminal frame of an answer (at most one per answer; may be sent before the provider stream is fully drained). Also sent for cancelled/superseded answers.

fields.name: finish_reason
fields.description: Provider finish reason ("stop", "length" when continuations are exhausted, "content_filter", any other provider value), "stop" when the provider gave none, "cancelled" (answer.stop), "superseded" (displaced by a newer question).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Answer id (always present on this endpoint).

frames.description: The server decided not to answer; terminal frame WITHOUT a preceding answer.start and without id. Sent for auto-triggered asks rejected by the interjection gate, for repeated empty asks, and when a pending gate decision is cancelled by a newer question.
Reply to `answer.stop` (sent after cancellation is requested; the cancelled answers' own answer.done "cancelled" frames may arrive before or after it).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Raw echo of the request's `id` value (string normally; null when the request had no id; echoed as-is even if not a string).

fields.name: count
fields.description: Number of live answers actually stopped (0 or 1 for a targeted stop).

frames.description: Refusal/error with a localized human message in the user's PROFILE language (users.language via i18n; clients display it verbatim). Connection-level errors (bad frames, forbidden, idle_timeout, internal crash, quota, rate limit, unsafe, transcription_unavailable, empty_question, responses_unavailable) carry no id; answer-terminal errors after answer.start (provider_error, internal, bad_image, vision_unavailable, vision_describer) carry the answer id. Shipped clients route an error without id to the pending answer page and leave the busy state on it.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Stable machine code: frame_too_large | bad_json | unknown_type | forbidden | idle_timeout | internal | empty_question | rate_limited | responses_unavailable | transcription_unavailable | vision_describer | vision_unavailable | bad_image | provider_error | minutes_exhausted (closed StrEnum RealtimeErrorCode, backend/src/meetassist/features/realtime/application/error_texts.py:67-117) plus `unsafe_request` (content-filter refusal, backend/src/meetassist/api/realtime_answer.py:660, backend/src/meetassist/api/realtime_vision.py:547).

fields.name: message
fields.description: Localized text for the user (16 languages; English when the profile language is null).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Answer id when the error terminates an answer that already got answer.start.

endpoints.auth_details: Bearer token (access JWT or device API key) in Authorization header, or `whisperer-bearer` subprotocol; plus ownership of the meeting session close(1008) before accept() -> client receives HTTP 403 (no token / invalid token, non-UUID session_id, foreign or missing session, per-user or per-worker socket cap). All four cases are indistinguishable by design (anti-IDOR).

query_params.name: session_id
query_params.description: PATH parameter (not query): meeting session UUID; must be owned by the caller.

endpoints.handshake: 1) extract token (header, else whisperer-bearer subprotocol) and resolve user -> else close 1008 pre-accept (HTTP 403). 2) parse session_id as UUID -> else 1008. 3) ownership check -> else 1008. 4) acquire per-user socket slot in the general pool (channel label `sessions`) -> else 1008. 5) accept() with no subprotocol. 6) join the Redis pub/sub room `rt:room:<session_id>` (if Redis is down the socket still works but receives no room events). 7) server sends personal `session.state` {status: active} (no seq). 8) read loop: each text frame parsed with json.loads and dispatched on `type`; 600 s without any client frame ends the connection. Room events are pushed concurrently by a relay task.
endpoints.resume: none. Pub/sub keeps no history: events published while disconnected are lost. Room events carry `seq`, a per-session Redis INCR counter (key rt:room:seq:<session_id>, TTL 30 min refreshed on every publish) shared across all processes, so a client can detect gaps; history is meant to be restored from the /v1/ws/realtime `transcript.restore` frame (other endpoint). Personal replies (session.state on connect, ack, pong) carry no seq.

close_codes.when: missing/invalid token
session_id is not a UUID
session not found or owned by another user
per-user (8) or per-worker (500) socket cap reached

idle timeout: no client frame for 600 s -> loop breaks and the handler returns without close(); also on malformed client input (non-JSON text, JSON that is not an object, binary frame) which raises out of the handler
Observed by the client when the handler returns or raises after accept() without calling close(): uvicorn closes the TCP transport without a close frame.
Client does not answer protocol-level pings: uvicorn default --ws-ping-interval 20 s / --ws-ping-timeout 20 s (not overridden in the launch command).
Server shutdown while the socket is open (uvicorn closes open websockets immediately on SIGTERM).
A single frame larger than --ws-max-size 12582912 bytes (12 MiB).

handshake_rejections.reason: HTTP 403 Forbidden instead of 101 (not a WS close code)
handshake_rejections.when: Any `ws.close(code=...)` issued BEFORE `ws.accept()`: uvicorn rejects the upgrade with HTTP 403, so the application close code (e.g. 1008) never reaches the client. Runtime: uvicorn[standard] (>=0.34; resolved 0.54 with websockets-sansio impl).

handshake_rejections.reason: HTTP 503 `draining` before upgrade (not a WS close code)
handshake_rejections.when: Process drain marker file (/app/.drain) present: DrainMiddleware refuses every NEW websocket handshake with HTTP 503 body `draining` (nginx retries it on another upstream only under /v1/ws/); if the server lacked the websocket.http.response extension it would send close 1013 pre-accept, i.e. HTTP 403.

frames.description: A transcript line produced by one of the user's devices. Re-broadcast to the whole room (including the sender) as a `transcript.delta` room event with the payload passed through VERBATIM (no validation), then a personal `ack` is sent.

fields.name: seq
fields.description: Client sequence number; echoed back as `ack.payload.client_seq` (null if absent).

fields.name: payload
fields.description: Opaque transcript payload, relayed as-is (default {}). Server-originated deltas use {speaker, text, at}.

frames.description: Announces an AI request. The server does NOT run anything; it only broadcasts `ai.stream.start` with execution_id `pending` to the room.

Translated audio from one of the owner's devices (e.g. iPhone) for another device (Mac with a virtual audio cable). Payload is neither parsed nor stored; it is broadcast verbatim to the room as `translation.audio`.

fields.name: payload
fields.description: Opaque audio payload defined by the native clients (default {}).

endpoints.handshake: 1) resolve user from token -> else 1008 pre-accept (HTTP 403). 2) decide accept subprotocol (`whisperer-bearer` iff token came via subprotocol). 3) validate `sid` -> else 1008 pre-accept. 4) acquire per-user slot (general pool) -> else accept + {t:error, code:retry_later} + close 1008. 5) voice gate + create voice_sessions row -> on refusal accept + {t:error, code} + close 1000. 6) accept(). 7) open Gemini Live session (model gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview, API v1alpha, server key) inside the shared Live-capacity slot. 8) send {t:ready, session_id}. 9) bidirectional relay until client disconnect, Gemini session end, 60 s of conversational inactivity, or model-requested farewell. 10) on normal end send {t:ended, reason}; on exception send {t:error, code:retry_later|voice_error}. 11) settle metering (wall clock since minted_at) and close() with 1000.
endpoints.resume: none at the socket level. Conversation memory lives server-side in the agent thread keyed by user_id + `sid`, so reconnecting with the same sid continues the dialogue (shared with text chat). Each connection mints a new voice_sessions metering row.

endpoints.handshake: 1) resolve user -> else 1008 pre-accept. 2) acquire general-pool slot -> else 1008 pre-accept. 3) accept (echo whisperer-bearer if used). 4) client sends hello within 15 s -> invalid: close 1008. 5) server stores presence presence:user:<id>:<conn_id> = {client, chat_session_id} with TTL 80 s. 6) server replays undelivered reminders for this channel as `reminder.due` frames (web channel: also seeds the Leo chat thread). 7) concurrently: forward live frames from Redis channel push:user:<user_id> (only reminder.due addressed to this channel and reminder.settled) and read client ping/ack. endpoints.resume: Durable delivery: every reminder has a proactive_deliveries row per channel (UNIQUE nudge_id+channel, statuses pending -> pushed -> acked/settled/failed/expired). On every hello the server replays open deliveries for the connecting channel: durable kinds (errand_due with evidence.explicit, mail_important, connection_broken, commitment_due), created in the last 24 h, unread, not held by quiet hours, not acked/settled by any channel, attempts < 10; max 20 nudges, oldest first; a desktop channel gets nothing while a web client is present. A background sweep re-publishes pushed-but-unacked deliveries after 30 s while the channel is present. Clients must ack each delivery_id; the first ack settles all other channels' deliveries and broadcasts reminder.settled.

endpoints.auth_details: none (anonymous landing-page demo); access is limited by a per-IP and platform-wide seconds budget Every refusal is AFTER accept: accept() (no subprotocol), send {t:error, code}, close 1008. Codes: translate_bad_mode | translate_bad_lang | translate_bad_voice | translate_disabled | visitor_limit | demo_unavailable.

query_params.name: mode
query_params.description: `classic` (turn-based engine gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview on API v1alpha, selectable voice) | `live` (continuous engine gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview on API v1beta, voice ignored). Trimmed and lower-cased; anything else -> translate_bad_mode.

query_params.name: target_lang
query_params.description: Target language, one of ru en de es fr zh pt it ja ko hi ar id tr vi th (trimmed, lower-cased); else translate_bad_lang.

query_params.name: voice
query_params.description: Synthesis voice for classic mode: `Zephyr` (default) | `Orus`, case-sensitive after trim; else translate_bad_voice.

endpoints.handshake: 1) build DemoSettings, resolve client IP. 2) validate mode/target_lang/voice and compute the session window = min(remaining budget for the mode, DEMO_TRANSLATE_MAX_SESSION_SECONDS=90) -> on DemoError: accept + {t:error, code} + close 1008. 3) Google Live key missing -> accept + {t:error, code:demo_unavailable} + close 1008. 4) accept(). 5) take a shared Live-capacity slot and connect Gemini Live for the mode. 6) send {t:ready, seconds:<window>}. 7) start the budget meter: charges 5 s AHEAD (Redis INCRBY on visitor and platform counters), sleeps 5 s, then sends {t:left, seconds}; repeats until the window is served or a charge is refused ({t:error, code:visitor_limit|platform_limit|counter_unavailable}). 8) relay audio/transcripts until client disconnect, Gemini close, meter end, or client receive timeout. 9) on exception send {t:error, code:busy|demo_unavailable}. 10) close(1000). No `ended` frame.
endpoints.resume: none. Budget is server-side per IP and per mode per UTC day; reconnecting starts a new session whose window is the remaining budget (capped at 90 s). Seconds charged ahead are not refunded on disconnect. GET /v1/demo/translate/budget (HTTP) returns the remaining seconds per mode.

close_codes.reason: policy violation, after accept, preceded by {t:error, code}
close_codes.when: bad mode/lang/voice, translation disabled, no budget left (visitor_limit)

close_codes.reason: policy violation, after accept, preceded by {t:error, code:demo_unavailable}
close_codes.when: Google Live API key not configured
end of every accepted session: window served, budget exhausted mid-session, client gone, Gemini closed, client receive timeout, or after {t:error} on failure
Observed by the client when the handler returns or raises after accept() without calling close(): uvicorn closes the TCP transport without a close frame.
Client does not answer protocol-level pings: uvicorn default --ws-ping-interval 20 s / --ws-ping-timeout 20 s (not overridden in the launch command).
Server shutdown while the socket is open (uvicorn closes open websockets immediately on SIGTERM).
A single frame larger than --ws-max-size 12582912 bytes (12 MiB).

handshake_rejections.reason: HTTP 403 Forbidden instead of 101 (not a WS close code)
handshake_rejections.when: Any `ws.close(code=...)` issued BEFORE `ws.accept()`: uvicorn rejects the upgrade with HTTP 403, so the application close code (e.g. 1008) never reaches the client. Runtime: uvicorn[standard] (>=0.34; resolved 0.54 with websockets-sansio impl).

handshake_rejections.reason: HTTP 503 `draining` before upgrade (not a WS close code)
handshake_rejections.when: Process drain marker file (/app/.drain) present: DrainMiddleware refuses every NEW websocket handshake with HTTP 503 body `draining` (nginx retries it on another upstream only under /v1/ws/); if the server lacked the websocket.http.response extension it would send close 1013 pre-accept, i.e. HTTP 403.
